KLM constants: K 0.20 s (average skilled typist, 55 wpm), P 1.10 s when no layout is given, H 0.40 s, B 0.10 s (Kieras, Using the Keystroke-Level Model to Estimate Execution Times, https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~kieras/docs/GOMS/KLM.pdf, opened 2026-09-29, a tutorial by a KLM author based on Card, Moran and Newell 1983); M 1.35 s (the top of the 0.6 to 1.35 s range Kieras gives; he recommends 1.2 s; applied to both flows). Kieras counts B for a press or a release (a click is BB, 0.2 s); these flows use one B per click on both sides, so a delta understates by 0.1 s per extra click on the side with more clicks; P with a layout uses Fitts, Shannon form MT = 0.37 + 0.13 * log2(D/W + 1) s (Cockburn et al. 2007 menu pointing profile), D centre to centre, W = smaller side of the target (assumption). Calibration: 8 right-handed graduate CS students, mouse, pointing down a 16-item vertical menu of 130x22 px items (items 1, 4, 8, 12, 16), so D up to about 340 px and ID up to about 4.0 bits (derived from the item size; the paper does not state distances). Terms with D above 350 px or ID above 4.0, and all 2D movements, are EXTRAPOLATED; the constant-P total is the primary result; PREDICTION band plus or minus 21 percent.

M policy: one M at the start of each cognitive unit and one before each variable string (KLM rules 1, 2 and 4); the same rule for current and proposed. Reading and judging are not modelled beyond one closing M.

R values: 200 ms for a client-side view change (view-class target, docs/hci/design/motion-and-performance.md), 300 ms for a local API round trip with re-render (commit-class target); both are assumptions, not measurements. Provider, verification and fixture waits are excluded from both sides because they are identical.
